svg.title: Initialize one repository: choose the matching route
svg.desc: Greenfield and brownfield are alternatives, not consecutive phases. Each has its own entry, scope and terminal result. Read the companion guide for conditions and all output details.

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono Variable, Consolas, Cascadia Mono, monospace

svg.text: INITIALIZATION • TWO ALTERNATIVES, NOT ONE SEQUENCE

text.font-family: Manrope Variable, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: New project: interview. Existing source: isolated evidence collection.

text.font-family: Manrope Variable, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Alternative 1: Initialize a new project from intent

svg.title: Initialize a new project from intent
svg.desc: Choose this route only when meaningful source does not yet exist. A decomposition persona is not an extra agent dispatch. Existing source selects the separate brownfield route. Actual endpoint: Populated project state, the three approved project-level Markdown documents, an initialization sentinel and no abandoned decomposition drafts. Code implementation and PR delivery are later work. Conditions and return paths remain in the companion reading view.

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono Variable, Consolas, Cascadia Mono, monospace
Manrope Variable, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Scaffold → interview → approve three documents → initialize

svg.title: Choose the new-project route
svg.desc: command: /ca:init: scaffold once → command: /ca:decompose: selected strategy → skill: decompose: establish or resume drafts. A writable project-state scaffold and a valid new-project interview or explicit resume choice. An initialized project is not reinitialized.

g.title: /ca:init: scaffold once. The scaffolder writes activation and empty state but no initialization sentinel. It refuses to overwrite existing state; an uninitialized stub enters its selected populator directly.

g.title: decompose: establish or resume drafts. Confirm pre-flight, explain the interview and inspect any existing draft session. Resume, restart and abort are user choices; do not silently delete prior drafts.

svg.title: Review three guiding documents
svg.desc: skill: decompose: complete each layer → skill: decompose: synthesize from disk → skill: decompose: iterate until approval. All three project-level documents are on disk and explicitly approved. Their tasks are not a typed feature execution plan.

user review: No population until all three outputs are approved.

g.title: decompose: complete each layer. Explore problem, users, capabilities, technical shape, integrations and risks. Persist completed layers and draft choices. Unresolved facts receive named questions instead of guesses.

svg.text: Alternative 2: Initialize existing code from evidence

svg.title: Initialize existing code from evidence
svg.desc: Choose this route when meaningful source exists. Six isolated scout reports are required; the orchestrator synthesizes their reports rather than loading raw source. Missing isolation is a capability stop. Actual endpoint: Populated source-backed project state, provenance and a code map, with each gap resolved or explicitly deferred before initialization. It does not invent the three greenfield planning documents. Conditions and return paths remain in the companion reading view.

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono Variable, Consolas, Cascadia Mono, monospace
Manrope Variable, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Scaffold → isolated scouts → resolve gaps → initialize

svg.title: Collect six bounded reports
svg.desc: command: /ca:init: scaffold once → command: /ca:create-context: selected strategy → skill: context-creation: confirm the source → agent: scout: six separate source slices. All six reports returned, including explicit not-found results. A missing report is not empty evidence and blocks synthesis.

validate source shape: The skill validates its own preconditions.
isolated slices: Dispatch every required scout before synthesis.

g.title: /ca:init: scaffold once. Create the enabled stub only when absent. Select the existing-code populator rather than treating the activation flag as completed initialization.

g.title: context-creation: confirm the source. Confirm meaningful code and identify its primary source directories. The general inline fallback cannot replace this route’s required isolated scouts.

g.title: scout: six separate source slices. Inspect stack, infrastructure, architecture, security, testing and data model in parallel. Return paths, lines, named values and content hashes, never secret values or raw code excerpts.

svg.title: Resolve the evidence gaps
svg.desc: skill: context-creation: report-only synthesis → skill: context-creation: resolve or defer → skill: context-creation: write project state. Real values are written from cited reports and explicit answers. Open uncertainty is recorded, not quietly upgraded to fact.

Manrope Variable, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif

path.title: missing facts: Only the needed user facts are asked, not a second greenfield interview.
resolved or deferred: Populate from reports and explicit answers without retaining placeholders as resolved values.

g.title: context-creation: report-only synthesis. Map the returned evidence into context, stack, standards and security drafts. Classify confidence; the orchestrator does not reopen raw source after the scout phase.

g.title: context-creation: resolve or defer. Ask the focused missing questions. Resolve each gap or explicitly defer it to open-questions before initialization; do not infer user decisions.

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono Variable, Consolas, Cascadia Mono, monospace
Manrope Variable, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif

g.title: context-creation: write project state. Write the surviving state documents and route board mutations through the helper. A release-target row is conditional on real evidence or a resolved declaration, not mandatory boilerplate.
